content: Ampicillin-sulbactam, marketed as UNASYN, is specifically indicated for the treatment of infections caused by susceptible strains of designated microorganisms in the conditions outlined below: Infections caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae (including beta-lactamase-producing strains). Infections caused by Proteus mirabilis. Infections caused by Staphylococcus aureus. Infections caused by Bacteroides species, including Bacteroides fragilis. Infections caused by Escherichia coli (including beta-lactamase-producing strains). It is important to note that the efficacy of UNASYN for certain organisms in specific organ systems has been studied in fewer than 10 infections. While UNASYN is indicated only for the conditions listed above, infections caused by organisms susceptible to ampicillin alone can also be treated with UNASYN due to its ampicillin component. Therefore, mixed infections involving ampicillin-susceptible organisms and beta-lactamase-producing organisms susceptible to UNASYN do not typically require the addition of another antibiotic. Before initiating treatment, appropriate culture and susceptibility tests should be performed to isolate and identify the causative organisms and determine their susceptibility to UNASYN. However, therapy may be started empirically before obtaining these results if there is a reasonable suspicion that the infection involves beta-lactamase-producing organisms listed above in the indicated organ systems. Once the results of bacteriological and susceptibility studies are available, therapy should be adjusted accordingly. To minimize the development of drug-resistant bacteria and maintain the effectiveness of UNASYN and other antibacterial agents, UNASYN should only be used to treat or prevent infections that are proven or strongly suspected to be caused by susceptible bacteria. When culture and susceptibility data are available, they should guide the selection or modification of antibacterial therapy. In the absence of such data, local epidemiological and susceptibility patterns should be considered to inform the empiric selection of therapy.
